title: Attention Is All You Need
experiment: Raising d_k with the 1/√d_k scaling switched off makes each attention row go from spread out to nearly one-hot, and the softmax gradients collapse. This is the effect §3.2.1 gives as the reason for scaling.
archetype_reason: scaled dot-product attention is a fixed chain of stages on a toy input (QKᵀ, then scale, then optional mask, then softmax, then ×V), and the intermediate logits and weights are the point

fixed.qkv_init: Q (seq_len×d_k), K (seq_len×d_k), V (seq_len×d_v) entries i.i.d. N(0, 1), drawn from a fixed-seed PRNG and redrawn when d_k changes
fixed.softmax_input: logits = QKᵀ, divided by √d_k when scaled is on; with causal mask, entries with key index > query index are set to -∞ before the softmax
fixed.statistics_over: all seq_len query rows; logit_std uses only the unmasked logits

metrics.name: max_weight
metrics.label: max weight
metrics.meaning: mean over the seq_len query rows of the largest softmax weight in that row

metrics.name: logit_std
metrics.label: logit std
metrics.meaning: population standard deviation of all unmasked softmax-input entries (QKᵀ, divided by √d_k when scaled is on)

metrics.name: softmax_grad
metrics.label: softmax gradient
metrics.meaning: mean over all unmasked entries (i, j) of p_ij·(1 − p_ij), the diagonal of the softmax Jacobian, where p_ij is the attention weight of query i on key j

reproduce.claim: With the 1/√d_k scaling, logits keep unit variance and attention stays spread out even at d_k = 512.
